Jordan / Marta —

Short answer: billing is based on the actual variant that served the request, plus the applicable per-call quantum/rounding. A couple of implementation notes and the proposal for Beacon:

- Effective-billing basis: If a request is routed to a 16k variant because the 32k pool is saturated, we bill tokens decoded by that 16k variant (including any prefix/response tokens).
- Round-to-quantum: We apply our per-call rounding quantum (100 tokens) on each request before summing across the invoice line. That means partial requests are rounded up to the nearest 100-token bucket.
- Streaming/truncation: For streaming sessions, we bill based on every emitted chunk; a truncated stream is billed only for chunks emitted, each chunk rounded to the quantum.
- KV/prefix caching: Cached prefix tokens are not recharged on every request; we credit reused KV tokens per our cache-credit rules (see attached calc).

Proposal for BeaconHealth (to avoid surprising invoice artifacts):
1) Provide a one-time credit for the first month to cover rounding noise (we've modeled this at $1,000 in the draft SOW).
2) Add explicit invoicing examples into the SOW appendix so procurement sees the worked math.

I've attached an internal calculation sheet (token_bucket_calc.xlsx) with sample lines. Ben — can you add a worked example for Jordan's invoice sample? Vanessa — flag if the SOW credit amount needs adjustment.

Cheers,
Kim

On Fri, May 31, 2029 at 10:22 Marta Ruiz <marta@beaconhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Kim — that helps. Two quick asks from procurement...

Jordan / Marta — here's a tight worked example you can paste into procurement: 

Scenario: client request with requested context 25,000 tokens; 32k pool saturated -> routed to 16k variant; stream emits 3 chunks (responses) before client aborts. Per-call quantum = 100 tokens. Unit price = $0.0006 per token (example).

Worked math (per-request):
- Requested context: 25,000 (not billed)
- Effective context served by 16k variant: 16,000 prefix + responses = 16,000 + 2,400 = 18,400 tokens emitted by the model
- Apply 100-token rounding per request/chunk: we assume the session produced total emitted tokens in three chunks: 800, 800, 800 (responses) + 16,000 prefix on initial call accounted as one chunk in this implementation example. Rounded chunks: 16,000 -> 16,000 (already multiple of 100), 800 -> 800, 800 -> 800, 800 -> 800. Total billed tokens = 16,000 + 2,400 = 18,400
- Charge = 18,400 * $0.0006 = $11.04

Invoice mapping (example):
1) Line item: Model inference (16k effective) — 18,400 tokens @ $0.0006 = $11.04
2) Credit: Rounding noise credit (one-time) -$1,000 (applied as separate invoice line)
3) Net line: $0.00 (for the first month after credit)

Notes:
- If a session were to route back to the 32k variant mid-stream, billing would switch to tokens emitted by that variant for subsequent chunks. We record variant per-chunk and bill accordingly.
- For prefix cache reuse we apply KV credits; the calc sheet models a scenario where repeated API calls inside a session only bill the decoded deltas.

Jordan, let me know if you'd like us to show this as per-call breakout in the invoice (we can itemize chunk-level rows) or keep a single aggregated line per session.

Cheers,
Ben
